introduction.p: The position of a car driving along a straight road at time t in minutes is given by the function y = s(t) that is pictured below. The car's position function has units measured in thousands of feet. For instance, the point (2, 4) on the graph indicates that after 2 minutes, the car has traveled 4000 feet.

statement.p:
Which option best describes the behavior of the car on the time interval [2,3]?
?
The car is stopped.
The car is traveling at a constant (nonzero) speed.
The car is accelerating.
The car is decelerating.

?
The car is stopped.

?
The car is stopped.

The car is accelerating.
The car is decelerating.
How many feet did the car travel on the time interval [5,7]?

Which of the following statements are true? Select all that apply.

li.p: When s'(t) is zero, the car is stopped.
When the car slows down, s'(t) is negative.
If s'(t) is zero, then s(t) must be zero.
The function s' represents the acceleration of the car.
When s'(t) is positive, the car's position is increasing.
When s'(t) is positive, the car's position is decreasing.
The function s' represents the velocity of the car.
None of the above statements are true.

statement.p: Which of the following statements are true? Select all that apply.

li.p: There are times when v'(t) is zero and v(t) is not zero.
When v'(t) is negative, the car is slowing down.
The function v' represents the position of the car.
If v'(t) is zero, then v(t) must be zero.
The function v' represents the acceleration of the car.
When v'(t) is negative, the car is moving backwards.
When v(t) is positive, v'(t) must also be positive.
None of the above statements are true.
